chunks.text: SF-049 Technip Energies UAE Reward Work Flow/Profile Badging R&R Sales Solution Given Closed Low Complexity Hemanga Solution Request 49 - Technip Energies UAE **Date:** 2025-06-13 | **Status:** Solution Given Closed | **Complexity:** Low Complexity Subject Solution Request for Technip energies UAE Brief Client has an R&R program that allows all employees a chance to vote for a peer colleague for a particular award nomination. Person with the highest nomination receives the award. Problem Description Let's consider there are two awards. Their current reward program involves every employee casting a vote for their peer colleague against an award. The employee with the highest number of votes against a particular award wins the award. Only single vote can be given against a particular award by an employee. We pitched profile badging in this case and also the idea of creating value based zero value awards instead of peer voting. And person receiving the highest number of times for award receives a profile badge with monetary value. However, can we have the limitation check of an employee giving only one award per quarter against an award? Solution Given Here's how we can structure it: Create Two Awards: A Zero Value Auto Approved Award (for peer nomination) A Quarterly Panel Award (which can be configured as a monetary award) Nomination Configuration: Assign the ‘Nominator’ role to all employees. Set a quota of 1 nomination per award per quarter for each nominator under the Zero Value Award. This ensures employees can only vote once per award each quarter. Progression Setup: Link the Zero Value Auto Approved Award to the Quarterly Panel Award through a progression workflow. All winners from the Zero Value Auto Approved Award will automatically progress to the Quarterly Panel Award. Panel Review: The Quarterly Panel Award will have two designated panelists to review the progressed nominee

chunks.text: SF-054 Antara Senior CAre Static Location info Implementation Solution Given Closed Medium Complexity Bhargav Solution Request 54 - Antara Senior CAre **Date:** 2025-06-23 | **Status:** Solution Given Closed | **Complexity:** Medium Complexity Subject Location Update Behavior in City API Brief When the location field is set as static in the 'My Profile' section, there is still another dropdown that allows users to change it as needed. Ideally, once a field is marked as static, there should be no alternate way for users to modify the same information. Problem Description When the location field is made static (non-editable) in the 'My Profile' section for all users on the platform, there is still another dropdown option available that allows users to select their location. When a user selects a location from this dropdown, it also updates the static location field accordingly. We want to ensure that certain employee details, which we receive through data integration, remain non-editable by users. Solution Given We’ve identified a scenario where the "Current Location" field below the 'My Profile' dropdown is calling the City API, and updates made here are overriding the Current City field in the 'My Profile' section, which should ideally be non editable for companies as per their configuration. To ensure flexibility while maintaining data consistency, we propose adding a configurable flag in the City API that supports two use cases: Restrictive Mode: When the location is fixed via client configuration, updates through the "Current Location" (outside 'My Profile') should be blocked. Flexible Mode: When the location is editable within 'My Profile', the same should be reflected or configurable via the "Current Location" selector outside the profile section. This will help us manage different client requirements and ensure alignment between displayed and editable fields. @Subhendu Go

Currently, when a recognition includes multiple recipients and one of them has enabled privacy settings (e.g., "Require my consent before recognitions are shown"), their name appears as "Anonymous User"—which is expected. However, if that anonymous user has a profile picture, the system currently shows it in a blurred format. MPAC would prefer a change to this behavior: Instead of displaying a blurred profile image for anonymous users, the platform should display the default avatar (as if no profile picture was uploaded at all). This change would: Avoid confusion caused by the blurred image (which draws unnecessary attention), Align better with user privacy expectations, Provide a cleaner and more consistent user experience. Let us know if this change is possible and if any additional information is needed. Solution Given There are three scenarios for profile picture display: Profile Picture Uploaded (No Consent Restrictions): The image is visible to all users. Consent Enabled (User Opts for Anonymity): The user appears as an "Anonymous User" with a randomly selected blurred placeholder image. These images are not linked to actual user photos and are used to maintain privacy, similar to practices on platforms like LinkedIn. No Profile Picture Uploaded: A default placeholder image is shown. chunks.text: SF-150 Weaver and Tidwell India LLP Display an informational warning like: “This nominee has already received an award” without restricting the nomination. CX Solution Given Closed Low complexity Nilimpa Solution Request 150 - Weaver and Tidwell India LLP **Date:** 2025-10-14 | **Status:** Solution Given Closed | **Complexity:** Low complexity Subject Solution request 155150::Weaver- Notification Message for Previously Awarded Nominees Brief Weaver- Notification Message for Previously Awarded Nominees Problem Description This is a requirement for the company Weaver. Weaver has cross-department awards. They want nominators to see a message indicating if a nominee has already received any awards in the past ( for a quarter ). Whenever a nominator initiates a new nomination, a message should appear below stating: “This nominee has already received an award.” (if applicable) However, this message should serve only as an informational warning — it should not restrict or prevent the nominator from proceeding with the nomination if they still wish to do so. In essence, the message is intended as a prompt for awareness, not a limitation. Solution Given The current system architecture does not support passive notifications. Key points include: Validation Flow Limitation: The system treats validations as hard stops; if a nominee has already received an award, the nomination process must be restarted. Flexibility in Nominations: Hard restrictions could block valid repeat recognitions, which goes against the inclusive intent of the program. Performance Concerns: Real-time checks for prior awards would increase system complexity and load. Alternative Option: If the goal is to restrict awards within a specific timeframe (e.g., one per quarter), that can be enforced via backend rules. Passive alerts without blocking nominations are not feasible in the current setup. Commercial Details - **Employee Size:** 250 - **Billing:** India - **Subscription Cost:** INR180000 - **Rewards Budget:*

However, the client would like to understand the in-depth details of how the calculation/conversion is handled by the system. I have informed the client that the system calculates the value based on the current exchange rate. As per my discussion with Subhendu, we update our exchange rates on a daily basis. The client has raised concerns with this approach, as fluctuations in the exchange rate may impact their budget. They have therefore requested us to check whether it is possible to incorporate static exchange values or explore any alternative approach, as they are not willing to proceed with the current process. Solution Given Exchange Rate Handling The system uses real-time exchange rates, updated daily, to convert points between currencies during transfers. Static exchange rates are not supported, as this could lead to inconsistencies and compliance issues. Impact on Billing Please note that exchange rate fluctuations do not affect client billing. Billing is always based on the original currency of allocation, regardless of where the points are transferred. When points are transferred, the system treats them as: Redeemed in the source country → billed to Infosys at the original currency value. Credited in the destination country → marked as non-billable points for future redemption. Example Scenario Suppose 1,000 points allocated in India (worth ₹1,000) are transferred to a user in the USA. Brief Customised award nomination workflow for annual awards for the client Bata. Problem Description Requirement Overview: Bata would like to configure an Annual Award within the platform. As part of the nomination process, they require a custom form to capture specific information related to the nominee’s KPIs and performance criteria. The details collected through the form will be used by leadership for evaluation. Proposed Flow: Nominator submits nomination for the Annual Award. Nominator selects the “Annual Award” category from the award list. Upon selection, a custom form appears where the nominator can provide required inputs related to predefined criteria (e.g., KPIs, achievements, performance highlights, etc.). Submitted form details are captured and shared with the CEO for review. CEO reviews the nominations along with the submitted form details. CEO selects and approves the top 3 winners based on the information provided in the form. Solution Given After reviewing the request, we would like to highlight that a custom nomination form that appears for the nominator during submission is currently not supported in the platform. However, the following alternative can be considered to achieve a similar outcome: Using the Recognition Message & Attachment The nominator can provide detailed information related to the nominee’s KPIs, achievements, and performance highlights in the Recognition Message section while submitting the nomination. Additionally, the nominator can upload a supporting document or form containing structured details as an attachment.

chunks.text: SF-260 Wasael Property Management Quota configuration Solution Given Closed Not Set Kongkana Solution Request 260 - Wasael Property Management **Date:** 2026-05-19 | **Status:** Solution Given Closed | **Complexity:** Not Set Subject Solution Request : 260260 : Wasael <> Project Wise Quota Configuration Brief Requirement for project-wise quota allocation or multiple quota assignment for a single HOD in the Shining Star award workflow. Problem Description The client requires flexibility in quota allocation for HODs managing multiple projects. Currently, for Shining Star award the quota is configured to be allocated as 1 quota per month to the HODs, which limits a single HOD to a fixed quota assignment. In this case, one HOD oversees three different projects and needs to approve three nominations, one for each project. So the client is requesting to check if we can enable project-wise quota allocation. Solution Given Create a separate Shining Star award for each project, with each award having its own dedicated monthly quota of 1. All ten awards will use different HOD as the approver except three awards which will use the same HOD as approver. Since quotas are maintained per approver per quota configuration, creating three separate quota configurations provides the HOD with three independent approval balances. As a result, approving a nomination for Project A will not affect the quotas for Projects B or C. Important: Each project award must have its own unique quota configuration. Multiple awards must not share the same quota configuration, as this would combine their balances into a single shared pool and remove the required segregation. Once the activity is done, disable the quota and disable the award. If required for different projects in ad-hoc basis, create new award and allocate the quota accordingly to the HOD. Commercial Details - **Employee Size:** 630

chunks.id: spec:Vantage Circle Bulk Award Points API v3.0 — Abstract Protocol Flow Diagram
chunks.title: Vantage Circle Bulk Award Points API v3.0 — Abstract Protocol Flow Diagram
chunks.text: Vantage Circle Bulk Award Points API v3.0 — Abstract Protocol Flow Diagram **Abstract Protocol Flow (OAuth 2.0)** The flow involves the following actors: - **Application (Client)** - **Vantage Circle (Resource Owner)** — for trusted parties this leg can be skipped. - **Authorization Server** and **Resource Server** — together forming the **Service API**. Steps shown in the diagram: 1. Authorization Request (Application → Vantage Circle) 2. Authorization Grant (Vantage Circle → Application) 3. Authorization Grant (Application → Authorization Server) 4. Access Token (Authorization Server → Application) 5. Access Token (Application → Resource Server) 6. Protected Resource (Resource Server → Application) Here is a more detailed explanation of the steps in the diagram: 1. The *application* requests authorization to access service resources from the *user*. 2. If the *user* authorized the request, the *application* receives an authorization grant. 3. The *application* requests an access token from the *authorization server* (API) by presenting authentication of its own identity, and the authorization grant. 4. If the application identity is authenticated and the authorization grant is valid, the *authorization server* (API) issues an access token to the application. Authorization is complete. 5. The *application* requests the resource from the *resource server* (API) and presents the access token for authentication. 6. If the access token is valid, the *resource server* (API) serves the resource to the *application*. Vantage Circle will provide the following identifiers — - **client_id** - **client_secret**

In this case **grant_type** will be **client_credentials** to get the **access_token**. - Pass the **client_id** in the body (which is used for client identification). - Pass the **client_secret** in the body.

chunks.id: spec:Vantage Circle Bulk Award Points API v3.0 — Body Parameters
chunks.title: Vantage Circle Bulk Award Points API v3.0 — Body Parameters
chunks.text: Vantage Circle Bulk Award Points API v3.0 — Body Parameters | Field Name | Data Type | Optional | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `grant_type` | String | NO | GRANT TYPE | | `client_id` | String | NO | CLIENT ID | | `client_secret` | String | NO | CLIENT SECRET | **CURL Example** ```bash curl -X POST \ https://partner-api.vantagecircle.in/v1/oauth2/access/token \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "grant_type": "client_credentials", "client_id": "xx", "client_secret": "xx" }' ``` **Success Response** ```json { "token_type": "Bearer", "access_token": "jaZ96DnmSuXKvdQfMqQAKjW8utWeAiKAQdzKbqgusP6xtId32H7xTci3tVaMskZb", "expires_in": 3600, "refresh_token": "9cbho9gMwkODSMknvwsnublqtpToulqlqQdq7iSTdTnq9lDuFlyfnvMjbi48xpSZ" } ``` **Response Details** - **token_type: "Bearer"** — Bearer Tokens are the predominant type of access token used with OAuth 2.0. - **access_token** — The access token is used for authentication and authorization to get access to the resources from the resource server. - **expires_in** — The lifetime in seconds of the access token. For example, the value "3600" denotes that the access token will expire in one hour from the time the response was generated. - **refresh_token** — The refresh token is used to get a new access token, when the old one expires. Instead of the normal grant type, the client provides the refresh token, and receives a new access token. **Error Responses** ```json { "err": "Unauthorized! Grant Type does not match." } ``` ```json { "err": "Unauthorized! Client Id not found." } ``` ```json { "err": "Unauthorized! Client Secret not found." } ``` ```json { "err": "Unauthorized! Client Id and Client Secret not found." } ```

chunks.text: Vantage Circle Gift Card API v1.0 — INTRODUCTION Welcome to the Vantage Circle Gift Card API documentation. The Vantage Circle Gift Card API allows you to order gift card(s) in a simple, programmatic way using conventional HTTP requests. The endpoints are intuitive and powerful, allowing you to easily make calls to retrieve information or to execute actions.

chunks.id: spec:Vantage Circle Gift Card API v1.0 — AUTHENTICATION / AUTHORIZATION
chunks.title: Vantage Circle Gift Card API v1.0 — AUTHENTICATION / AUTHORIZATION
chunks.text: Vantage Circle Gift Card API v1.0 — AUTHENTICATION / AUTHORIZATION Vantage Circle will provide the following identifiers which will be needed for API authentication. ``` public_key private_key ``` **Important Note** *public_key and hash_key are required for all API calls which will be needed to be passed in the headers.* Pass `public_key` in the header (which is used for client identification). Use `private_key` to generate a HMAC hash (`hash_key`) which is used to verify data integrity. Refer to the process below to generate a HMAC hash. **How to generate a hash_key?** In order to generate a hash key, create a HMAC hash. Please find the details below: Use the `private_key` and message (which can be the json encoded format of the data passed if POST API or an empty string passed if GET API) with the MD5 algorithm to generate a hash.

chunks.id: spec:Vantage Circle Gift Card API v1.0 — Example 1 - For calling the GET API to fetch products:
chunks.title: Vantage Circle Gift Card API v1.0 — Example 1 - For calling the GET API to fetch products:
chunks.text: Vantage Circle Gift Card API v1.0 — Example 1 - For calling the GET API to fetch products: ``` private_key : xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx ``` Take the query parameters as the message. In case, there is no query parameter, it will be `""` (an empty string). Generate the hash using the `private_key` and message. Algorithm used : MD5

chunks.id: spec:Vantage Circle Gift Card API v1.0 — Example 2 - For calling the POST API to create an order:
chunks.title: Vantage Circle Gift Card API v1.0 — Example 2 - For calling the POST API to create an order:
chunks.text: Vantage Circle Gift Card API v1.0 — Example 2 - For calling the POST API to create an order: ``` private_key : xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx ``` Message: (json encoded), for example - ```json { "client_reference" : "90bJIU90hI889iw", "product_id" : 10615, "amount" : 500, "quantity" : 1, "country_id" : 91, "currency_code" : "INR", "delivery_method" : "api", "receiver_email" : "", "email_subject" : "", "email_template" : "", "notification_email" : "" } ``` Generate the hash using the `private_key` and message. Algorithm used : MD5 The hash key can also be generated at the following url: https://codebeautify.org/hmac-generator While generating the hash at the above mentioned url, the json body should be exactly in the following format: ```json {"client_reference":"90bJIU90hI8k9iw","product_id":10615,"amount":500,"quantity":1,"country_id":91,"currency_code":"INR","delivery_method":"api","receiver_email":"","email_subject":"","email_template":"","notification_email":""} ``` ---

Access Token ┌──────────────────────┐ │ │ │ ───────────────────────────────────► │ Resource Server │ ┘ │ │ ◄─────────────────────────────────── │ │ └──────────────┘ 6. Protected Resource └──────────────────────┘ ``` Here is a more detailed explanation of the steps in the diagram: 1. The *application* requests authorization to access service resources from the *user* 2. If the *user* authorized the request, the *application* receives an authorization grant 3. The *application* requests an access token from the *authorization server* (API) by presenting authentication of its own identity, and the authorization grant 4. If the application identity is authenticated and the authorization grant is valid, the *authorization server* (API) issues an access token to the application. Authorization is complete. 5. The *application* requests the resource from the *resource server* (API) and presents the access token for authentication 6. If the access token is valid, the *resource server* (API) serves the resource to the *application* Vantage Circle will provide the following identifiers - - **client_id** - **client_secret**

Instead of the normal grant type, the client provides the refresh token and receives a new access token.

chunks.id: spec:Partner OAuth2 API Reference
chunks.title: Partner OAuth2 API Reference
chunks.text: Partner OAuth2 API Reference Partner OAuth2 API Reference Integrate with Vantage Circle to authenticate your users and access their profile and lead data using the OAuth2 Authorization Code Grant flow.

chunks.id: spec:Partner OAuth2 API Reference — Overview
chunks.title: Partner OAuth2 API Reference — Overview
chunks.text: Partner OAuth2 API Reference — Overview The integration is a two-step flow. After the user completes the Vantage Circle login/consent screen and is redirected back to your `redirect_uri` with an authorization code, your server performs the following calls: | | Call | Purpose | |---|------|---------| | 1 | `POST /v2/oauth2/access/token` | exchange `code` for `access_token` | | 2 | `POST /v2/oauth2/user/info` | use `access_token` to fetch user profile | | 3 | `POST /v2/oauth2/refresh/token` | renew expired `access_token` using `refresh_token` | > **Credentials:** Your `client_id`, `client_secret`, permitted `grant_types`, and registered `redirect_uri` are provisioned by Vantage Circle. Contact your POC to obtain them.

chunks.id: spec:Partner OAuth2 API Reference — Authentication
chunks.title: Partner OAuth2 API Reference — Authentication
chunks.text: Partner OAuth2 API Reference — Authentication Token endpoints authenticate your client using HTTP Basic credentials passed as a Base64-encoded `Authorization` header: **FORMAT** ``` Authorization: Bearer base64(<client_id>:<client_secret>) ``` Encode `client_id:client_secret` as a single Base64 string and pass it as `Bearer <encoded>` in the `Authorization` header.

chunks.id: spec:Partner OAuth2 API Reference — Token Lifecycle
chunks.title: Partner OAuth2 API Reference — Token Lifecycle
chunks.text: Partner OAuth2 API Reference — Token Lifecycle | Authorization Code | Access Token | Refresh Token | |--------------------|--------------|---------------| | **One-time** | **1 hour** | **1 year** | | Issued by VC redirect. Single use only. | Used to call user info. Renew with refresh token. | Exchanges for a new access token. No re-login needed. |

chunks.title: Partner OAuth2 API Reference — Step 1 — Exchange Authorization Code for Access Token
chunks.text: Partner OAuth2 API Reference — Step 1 — Exchange Authorization Code for Access Token After the user is redirected back to your `redirect_uri` with a `code` query parameter, exchange it for an access token and refresh token. ``` POST /v2/oauth2/access/token ```

chunks.title: Partner OAuth2 API Reference — Example Request
chunks.text: Partner OAuth2 API Reference — Example Request **CURL** ```bash curl --request POST '{base_url}/v2/oauth2/access/token' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer <base64(client_id:client_secret)>' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \ --data-urlencode 'grant_type=authorization_code' \ --data-urlencode 'code=<authorization_code>' \ --data-urlencode 'redirect_uri=<your_registered_redirect_uri>' ``` **200 OK** ```json { "token_type": "Bearer", "access_token": "Vy92FD4tWvpc20HmSqNIbyraSTFVYQKDaaE3qrn5RCAvjWnte7I9sDkBFZdFK0gb", "expires_in": 3600, "refresh_token": "5jCKKqNQ7BmdVSQ8FUhAdJbg2k297SwyDx8jWczTYxeu3GVGMEyLecHohNOX2TOK" } ```

Valid for 1 hour. Pass to Step 2. | | `expires_in` | integer | Seconds until the access token expires | | `refresh_token` | string | 64-character token. Valid for 1 year. chunks.text: Partner OAuth2 API Reference — Step 2 — Fetch User Information Using the `access_token` from Step 1, retrieve the authenticated user's profile. If your client was provisioned with the `leads:share` scope, a `lead_share` object is included in the response. ``` POST /v2/oauth2/user/info ```

The exact fields returned within `lead_share` depend on the configuration agreed upon with Vantage Circle for your deal.

chunks.id: spec:Partner OAuth2 API Reference — Example Request
chunks.title: Partner OAuth2 API Reference — Example Request
chunks.text: Partner OAuth2 API Reference — Example Request **CURL** ```bash curl --request POST '{base_url}/v2/oauth2/refresh/token' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer <base64(client_id:client_secret)>' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \ --data-urlencode 'grant_type=refresh_token' \ --data-urlencode 'refresh_token=5jCKKqNQ7BmdVSQ8FUhAdJbg2k297SwyDx8jWczTYxeu3GVGMEyLecHohN' ``` **200 OK** ```json { "token_type": "Bearer", "access_token": "<new_access_token>", "expires_in": 3600, "refresh_token": "5jCKKqNQ7BmdVSQ8FUhAdJbg2k297SwyDx8jWczTYxeu3GVGMEyLecHohNOX2TOK" } ``` > The `refresh_token` in the response is the same one you sent. A new one is not issued. If the refresh token itself expires (after 1 year), the user must complete the VC login/consent flow again.

chunks.text: Vantage Circle — Partner Brand Integration (OAuth2) API v2.0 — Workflow Diagram **BRAND STORE REDIRECTION WORKFLOW** 1. User clicks **GET OFFER / REDIRECT** at Vantage Circle Platform. 2. VC redirects the user to Brand Store's Redirect URL with `authorization_code`. 3. Brand Store invokes VC APIs: 1. GET `access_token` by `authorization_code` 2. GET user info by `access_token` 4. Brand Store successfully registers/logs in the user. ---

chunks.title: Vantage Circle — Partner Brand Integration (OAuth2) API v2.0 — Get the access_token by authorization_code
chunks.text: Vantage Circle — Partner Brand Integration (OAuth2) API v2.0 — Get the access_token by authorization_code `grant_type`, `code` along with `redirect_uri` will be required to be passed in the post body in the form of `form-data(x-www-form-urlencoded)` in order to get the `access_token`. - Pass the `client_id` and `client_secret` in the headers encoded with Base64. Format: `base64encode(<client-id>:<client-secret>)` - Pass the `grant_type` in the form data. In this case `grant_type` will be `authorization_code` to get the `access_token`. - Pass the `code` in the form data. (can be retrieved from the redirect url once the user is redirected from Vantage Circle site). - Pass the `redirect_uri` in the form data. (Partner Client has to provide this URL)

chunks.id: spec:Vantage Circle — Partner Brand Integration (OAuth2) API v2.0 — Response Details
chunks.title: Vantage Circle — Partner Brand Integration (OAuth2) API v2.0 — Response Details
chunks.text: Vantage Circle — Partner Brand Integration (OAuth2) API v2.0 — Response Details - **`token_type: "Bearer"`** — Bearer Tokens are the predominant type of access token used with OAuth 2.0. - **`access_token`** — The access token is used for authentication and authorization to get access to the resources from the resource server. - **`expires_in`** — The lifetime in seconds of the access token. For example, the value "3600" denotes that the access token will expire in one hour from the time the response was generated. - **`refresh_token`** — The refresh token is used to get a new access token, when the old one expires. Instead of the normal grant type, the client provides the refresh token, and receives a new access token.

chunks.title: Vantage Circle — Partner Redemption API v1.0 — Abstract Protocol Flow Diagram
chunks.text: Vantage Circle — Partner Redemption API v1.0 — Abstract Protocol Flow Diagram ``` Abstract Protocol Flow (OAuth 2.0) +-------------+ 1. Authorization Request +------------------------+ For trusted parties | | -----------------------------> | Vantage Circle | this leg can be | | 2. Authorization Grant | (Resource Owner) | skipped. | | <----------------------------- +------------------------+ | | | Application | 3. Authorization Grant +------------------------+ | (Client) | -----------------------------> | Authorization Server | | | 4. Access Token | | | | <----------------------------- +------------------------+ Service API | | | | 5. Access Token +------------------------+ | | -----------------------------> | Resource Server | | | 6. Protected Resource | | | | <----------------------------- +------------------------+ +-------------+ ``` Here is a more detailed explanation of the steps in the diagram: 1. The *application* requests authorization to access service resources from the *user* 2. If the *user* authorized the request, the *application* receives an authorization grant 3. The *application* requests an access token from the *authorization server* (API) by presenting authentication of its own identity, and the authorization grant 4. If the application identity is authenticated and the authorization grant is valid, the *authorization server* (API) issues an access token to the application. Authorization is complete. 5. The *application* requests the resource from the *resource server* (API) and presents the access token for authentication 6. If the access token is valid, the *resource server* (API) serves the resource to the *application* Vantage Circle will provide the following identifiers - - **client_id** - **client_secret**

chunks.text: Vantage Circle — Partner Redemption API v1.0 — Body Parameters | Field Name | Data Type | Optional | Description | |---|---|---|---| | grant_type | String | NO | GRANT TYPE | | client_id | String | NO | CLIENT ID | | client_secret | String | NO | CLIENT SECRET | **CURL Example** ```bash curl -X POST \ https://partner-api.vantagecircle.in/v1/oauth2/access/token \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "grant_type": "client_credentials", "client_id": "xx", "client_secret": "xx" }' ``` **Success Response** ```json { "token_type": "Bearer", "access_token": "jaZ96DnmSuXKvdQfMqQAKjW8utWeAiKAQdzKbqgusP6xtId32H7xTci3tVaMskZb", "expires_in": 3600, "refresh_token": "9cbho9gMwkODSMknvwsnublqtpToulqlqQdq7iSTdTnq9lDuFlyfnvMjbi48xpSZ" } ``` **Response Details** - **token_type: "Bearer"** - Bearer Tokens are the predominant type of access token used with OAuth 2.0. - **access_token** - The access token is used for authentication and authorization to get access to the resources from the resource server. - **expires_in** - The lifetime in seconds of the access token. For example, the value "3600" denotes that the access token will expire in one hour from the time the response was generated. - **refresh_token** - The refresh token is used to get a new access token, when the old one expires. Instead of the normal grant type, the client provides the refresh token, and receives a new access token. **Error Responses** ```json { "err": "Unauthorized! Grant Type does not match." } ``` ```json { "err": "Unauthorized! Client Id not found." } ``` ```json { "err": "Unauthorized! Client Secret not found." } ``` ```json { "err": "Unauthorized! Client Id and Client Secret not found." } ```

chunks.text: Vantage Circle — Points ⇄ Currency Conversion Rates (Reference) Vantage Circle — Points ⇄ Currency Conversion Rates (Reference) > **Purpose:** Give this file to an AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT, etc.) as context. It contains everything needed to answer: *"For client X in country Y, how many points equal 1 unit of currency?"* and to convert points ⇄ money. > **As of:** 2026-07-10 · derived from platform configuration + empirically validated against **2.19M gift-card redemptions (Nov 2024 – Jun 2026)** with **zero contradictions**. ---

chunks.id: spec:Vantage Circle — Points ⇄ Currency Conversion Rates (Reference) — 1. How conversion works
chunks.title: Vantage Circle — Points ⇄ Currency Conversion Rates (Reference) — 1. How conversion works
chunks.text: Vantage Circle — Points ⇄ Currency Conversion Rates (Reference) — 1. How conversion works - Formula: **`currency_amount = points ÷ points_per_unit`** (so `points_per_unit` = points needed for 1 unit of currency). - Rate resolution order: 1. **Explicit client rule** — a per-client (sometimes per-country) override configured in the application. 2. **Country default** — if no client rule exists, the country's default `points_per_unit` applies (Section 3). Defaults are always 1, 10, or 100. - **Cross-currency (FX-linked) redemptions:** points are pegged to the employee's *home* currency. If they redeem in a different currency (usually USD/EUR), the observed ratio = home peg × FX rate of that day, so it varies. Example: Amdocs Mexico peg is 1 pt = 1 MXN; a USD gift card therefore costs ≈17–19 pts per $1 (the MXN/USD rate). Rows marked `FX` below are of this kind — quote the peg, not a fixed cross rate.

chunks.title: Vantage Circle — Points ⇄ Currency Conversion Rates (Reference) — 5. Caveats for the AI using this file
chunks.text: Vantage Circle — Points ⇄ Currency Conversion Rates (Reference) — 5. Caveats for the AI using this file - A client-country pair absent from Section 4 has never had a redemption and has no known override → **assume the country default (Section 3)**, and say so. - Treat rates with fewer than ~10 txns as low-confidence; prefer the client's stated policy line. - `FX` rows: do NOT quote the listed ratio as fixed — it changes daily. Quote the home-currency peg and note the conversion floats with FX. - Rates are points-side conversions only; they say nothing about margins, vendor costs, or FX fees. - Data window ends 30 Jun 2026 (ledger) / Jul 2026 (configuration snapshot). Rates can be reconfigured by the client at any time. *Generated from the Vantage Circle redemption ledger + application rate rules. Internal use.*

chunks.title: SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration
chunks.text: SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration Step-by-step guide for configuring SCIM 2.0 automated user provisioning between Azure Active Directory and Vantage Circle.

chunks.id: spec:SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration — Architecture
chunks.title: SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration — Architecture
chunks.text: SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration — Architecture The System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) specification is designed to make managing user identities in cloud-based applications easier. Azure AD acts as the Identity Provider (IdP) and pushes user data to Vantage Circle via standard SCIM 2.0 REST operations (GET, POST, PATCH, PUT, DELETE) over the `/Users` endpoint. | Component | Role | |---|---| | Azure Active Directory | Identity Provider — source of user records | | SCIM 2.0 Connector | Translates Azure AD provisioning actions to REST calls | | Vantage Circle | Service Provider — receives and stores user data |

chunks.id: spec:SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration — Authentication
chunks.title: SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration — Authentication
chunks.text: SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration — Authentication Azure AD uses **Bearer Token** (Secret Token) authentication for SCIM provisioning. | Field | Value | |---|---| | Authentication Method | Bearer Token (Base64-encoded) | | Secret Token | Provided by Vantage Circle POC | | User Attributes | Provided by Vantage Circle POC | | **Token Format** | Secret Token = `Base64("username:password")` — the Base64 string of your VC-issued credentials. Azure sends this as `"Authorization: Bearer <token>"` and the VC SCIM endpoint decodes it as Basic Auth. | > **Note:** All required details — Tenant URL, Secret Token, and user attributes — will be provided by the Vantage Circle POC.

chunks.title: SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration — STEP 1 — Create an Enterprise Application in Azure AD
chunks.text: SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration — STEP 1 — Create an Enterprise Application in Azure AD Sign in to the Azure Portal and navigate to **Azure Active Directory → Enterprise Applications → New Application**. Select "Create your own application", enter a name (e.g. Vantage Circle), choose "Integrate any other application you don't find in the gallery (Non-gallery)", and click Create. | Field | Value | |---|---| | App Name | Vantage Circle (or any name chosen by the client) | | Application Type | Non-gallery (Integrate any other application) |

chunks.id: spec:SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration — STEP 2 — Configure Provisioning — Enter Admin Credentials
chunks.title: SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration — STEP 2 — Configure Provisioning — Enter Admin Credentials
chunks.text: SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration — STEP 2 — Configure Provisioning — Enter Admin Credentials Inside the newly created application, navigate to **Provisioning** in the left menu. Click "Get started", set Provisioning Mode to Automatic, then expand Admin Credentials and enter the Tenant URL and Secret Token provided by the Vantage Circle POC. | Field | Value | |---|---| | Provisioning Mode | Automatic | | Tenant URL | `https://scim.vantagecircle.com/api/v1/scim` | | Secret Token | Provided by Vantage Circle POC |

chunks.id: spec:SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration — STEP 3 — Test the Connection and Save
chunks.title: SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration — STEP 3 — Test the Connection and Save
chunks.text: SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration — STEP 3 — Test the Connection and Save Click **Test Connection** to verify that Azure AD can reach the Vantage Circle SCIM endpoint. A success message confirms the credentials are valid. Click Save to persist the configuration. | Capability | Supported | |---|---| | Create Users | Yes | | Update User Attributes | Yes — via PUT only. Azure sends updates as PATCH which is not currently supported (returns 405). Attribute updates require a full PUT request. | | Deactivate Users | Yes — via DELETE or PUT (active=false). Azure delivers deactivations as PATCH (returns 405). Manual deactivation via DELETE works correctly. | | Import Users | No — VC is Service Provider only. Read endpoints exist solely for Azure matching; no inbound sync-back path. | | Push Groups | No |

chunks.id: spec:SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration — STEP 4 — Configure Provisioning Settings
chunks.title: SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration — STEP 4 — Configure Provisioning Settings
chunks.text: SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration — STEP 4 — Configure Provisioning Settings Under the Settings section, set the Scope to "Sync only assigned users and groups" so that only users explicitly assigned to the application are provisioned to Vantage Circle. Optionally enable email notifications for provisioning failures. | Setting | Recommended Value | |---|---| | Provisioning Mode | Automatic | | Scope | Sync only assigned users and groups | | Send email notification on failure | Enabled (recommended) | | Provision Azure Active Directory Users | Yes | | Provision Azure Active Directory Groups | No |

chunks.id: spec:SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration — STEP 5 — Configure Attribute Mappings
chunks.title: SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration — STEP 5 — Configure Attribute Mappings
chunks.text: SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration — STEP 5 — Configure Attribute Mappings Click "Provision Azure Active Directory Users" under the Mappings section. Review and configure the attribute mappings to ensure the fields required by Vantage Circle are correctly mapped from Azure AD. Add any custom attributes provided by the Vantage Circle POC. | Azure AD Attribute | Vantage Circle Attribute | Notes / Code Verdict | |---|---|---| | `userPrincipalName` | `userName` | **1 (Primary)** Verified. Used as login and email. Filter matching currently broken — surrounding quotes prevent `userName eq "..."` from matching stored login. See Known Limitations 2. | | `givenName` | `name.givenName` | **Required** Required field. Provisioning fails with HTTP 500 if omitted from the Azure payload. Ensure givenName is always mapped. | | `surname` | `name.familyName` | **Required** Required field. Provisioning fails with HTTP 500 if omitted. Ensure surname/familyName is always mapped. | | `mail` | `emails[type eq "work"].value` | — Parsed by VC but not stored. Vantage Circle keys off userName (UPN) as the email address. This field has no effect unless UPN differs from mail. | | `Switch([IsSoftDeleted], ...)` | `active` | — Read correctly. However, deactivation (active=false) is delivered by Azure as PATCH, which returns 405. Only takes effect via DELETE or PUT. See Known Limitations 1. | | `[ custom attributes ]` | `[ as provided by VC POC ]` | — Supported via enterprise extension: `department`, `employeeNumber`, `gender`, `city`, `employeeId`, `reportingManager`, `gradeGroup`, `dob`, `doj`. |

chunks.id: spec:SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration — STEP 6 — Assign Users and Groups to the Application
chunks.title: SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration — STEP 6 — Assign Users and Groups to the Application
chunks.text: SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration — STEP 6 — Assign Users and Groups to the Application Navigate to **Users and groups** in the left menu. Click Add user/group, search for and select the users or Azure AD groups that should be provisioned to Vantage Circle, then click Assign. | Object Type | How to Assign | |---|---| | Individual User | Add user/group → search by name or email → Assign | | Azure AD Group | Add user/group → search for group name → Assign |

chunks.id: spec:SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration — STEP 7 — Turn Provisioning Status to "On"
chunks.title: SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration — STEP 7 — Turn Provisioning Status to "On"
chunks.text: SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration — STEP 7 — Turn Provisioning Status to "On" Return to the Provisioning page. Toggle the Provisioning Status to On and click Save. Azure AD will begin an initial sync cycle, creating all assigned users in Vantage Circle. Subsequent incremental cycles run automatically every ~40 minutes. | Action | Description | |---|---| | Provisioning Status → On | Starts the initial full sync cycle | | View provisioning logs | Monitor sync progress and errors | | Restart provisioning | Re-triggers a full sync if needed | > **Note:** The initial sync may take some time depending on the number of users. Monitor progress via View provisioning logs to check for any errors.

chunks.id: spec:SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration — Endpoint Reference
chunks.title: SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration — Endpoint Reference
chunks.text: SCIM 2.0 — Microsoft Azure AD Integration — Endpoint Reference The following SCIM 2.0 endpoints are available on the Vantage Circle SCIM server. All endpoints require Basic Auth (Bearer Token = Base64-encoded credentials). | Method | Path | Handler | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `GET` | `/api/v1/scim/Users/:id` | `fetchUser` | Fetch a single user by internal ID | | `GET` | `/api/v1/scim/Users` | `fetchUsers` | List users or filter by userName (Azure test-connection) | | `POST` | `/api/v1/scim/Users` | `createUser2` | Create a new user; deduplicates by email + companyId | | `PUT` | `/api/v1/scim/Users/:id` | `updateUser2` | Full update of an existing user by email | | `DELETE` | `/api/v1/scim/Users/:id` | `deleteUser` | Deactivate a user (sets status=false) | | `GET` | `/api/v1/scim/ServiceProviderConfig` | `fetchServiceProviderConfig` | Returns static SCIM capability config | | `GET` | `/api/v1/scim/ResourceTypes` | `fetchResourceTypes` | Returns supported resource type definitions | > **Note:** No PATCH route exists. Azure provisioning actions that use PATCH (attribute updates and deactivations) will return HTTP 405.

chunks.id: blueprint:External Recognition Platform → VC Redemption Backend
chunks.title: External Recognition Platform → VC Redemption Backend
chunks.text: External Recognition Platform → VC Redemption Backend Rewards & Redemption / API Integration Companies running their own recognition platform with no redemption catalog api bulk-award-points sso redemption gift-cards External Recognition Platform → VC Redemption Backend Use Case A prospect already runs recognition on their own platform and already issues points to employees. They have no redemption catalog and no intent to build fulfilment. They want Vantage Circle to sit behind their platform as the place points turn into rewards. Their recognition layer stays untouched. The only real decisions are **where the wallet lives** and **who owns the redemption screen** — those two answers drive ~90% of the build effort on both sides. Solution Overview Three options. Recommend A, keep B available permanently, deprioritise C. | Option | Wallet lives | Redemption screen | They build | Time to live | Verdict | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | **A · Points push + SSO** | Vantage Circle | VC platform | One API call + SSO | 2–4 weeks | **Recommend** | | **B · Manual upload + SSO** | Vantage Circle | VC platform | SSO only | Days | Always available | | **C · Embedded gift cards** | Their side | Their UI | Catalog, checkout, fulfilment | Quarter+ | Phase 2 | A and B share one destination — only how points get in differs. B is not a throwaway prototype; it is A with a human standing in for one API call. Nothing is rebuilt on graduation. Components Option A — Points push + SSO (recommended) - [ ] `POST /v1/award/bulkpoints` fired per recognition event - [ ] "Redeem now" link in the award email they already send
